trigger: operator follows the README literally: apt-mark hold + Package-Blacklist stanza, later runs only the documented release step `apt-mark unhold` after the monthly review
classification_rationale: missing release step for a config the doc itself introduces: the doc names only apt-mark unhold, so the blacklist entry (invisible to apt-mark showhold) keeps the unattended job skipping the package
summary: docs-writer derived I7/E3 MEDIUM. release-deploy (rd-1) derived HIGH (I7 raised: omission conceals withheld security updates; I4 same band) and flagged disagreement. An independent adjudicator (general-purpose Sonnet, agent aade647f5922906e0) read the preamble literally: I7 does not raise (the doc discloses the security-update cost at L113; the stale entry only affects the unattended job, is greppable, manual apt upgrade and CI apt-get still work), I4 rejected: derived MEDIUM/SHOULD, not BLOCKING. Redundancy: release-deploy verified on another Ubuntu box that unattended-upgrade skips held packages itself, so the stanza adds nothing. Fix: delete the stanza or add 'also remove the Package-Blacklist entry' to the release step.

trigger: a hold or blacklist outlives the 'suggested: monthly' review because the README names no owner, tracker, expiry or durable record, and nothing alerts on hold age

summary: Reported by up-6 (MEDIUM/SHOULD), sre-2 (MEDIUM/SHOULD), rd-4 (LOW), co-1 (LOW; compliance-officer notes CC7.1/CC8.1 evidence gap, native would be MEDIUM). The recorded facts (I8, E0) derive LOW; the SHOULD label is the stronger and is kept (label governs when stronger than the facts are recorded; no de-escalation). Not BLOCKING: the doc discloses the debt cost (same weighing as doc-1 adjudication). Fix: name an owner role + a tracking issue; require a record per hold (package, version, reason, owner, date, expiry); say monthly review is unenforced.

trigger: the flood child emits nothing or fails to exec (awk missing/broken alternatives link): CHECK(lines.size()<=16) and <1000 pass vacuously

summary: Reported by quality-engineer (qe-1), cpp-safety (cps-1), unhappy-path (up-2 adds that BR-004 then fails as 0==500 with no spawn_error shown). MUTATION RESULT (standalone harness, real lib, mutated child; the prebuilt test binary cannot be recompiled): print "xx" -> sec-7 passes (10 lines) and cap1000 passes, BR-004 detects via lines[0]=="x"; print "x\r" undetected (runner strips CR); 64-byte lines sec-7 passes (1 line). So sec-7 does NOT detect a broken 2-byte-line assumption (it is bound by bytes/count by design; the 2-byte width is asserted nowhere, qe-2 INFO). Fix: add CHECK(result.output_truncated) or CHECK(!result.lines.empty()) to sec-7.

trigger: a future regression of the post-latch over-cap behaviour that #5298/#5306 fixed
classification_rationale: BR-004's awk flood is pipe-bound, so it can no longer push post-latch bytes past the 1,000,000-byte cap before the kill (as the uutils yes did); it still spans >=2 512-byte reads so the cross-read latch is exercised
summary: The over-cap condition is now covered only by the deterministic awk_head_then_flood tests (L714-790; cpp-expert confirmed the L733 comment is accurate and that test uses awk). Not a regression of coverage per se; recorded so the trade-off is visible.
